exposure: time from positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR NP swab to delivery
outcome: transfer rate of SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies to newborns
SARS-CoV-2 IgG concentrations in maternal and umbilical cord sera
cohort: The study included 99 women who had a SARS-CoV-2 PCR-positive nasopharyngeal swab or a household member with a positive swab during pregnancy or at labor, or COVID-19 symptoms upon admission, along with their infants.
finding: A strong correlation was found between SARS-CoV-2 IgG concentrations in maternal and umbilical cord sera, with transfer ratios exceeding 1.0 in the majority of seropositive mother-infant dyads, and transfer was proportional to the time from infection to delivery.
